text: Write two classes differing only in whether they override `hashCode`, and put equal objects in a set. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static class Good { final int x,y; Good(int x,int y){this.x=x;this.y=y;}
@Override public boolean equals(Object o){ return o instanceof Good g && g.x==x && g.y==y; }
static class Bad { final int x,y; Bad(int x,int y){this.x=x;this.y=y;}
Set<Good> good = new HashSet<>(); good.add(new Good(1,2)); good.add(new Good(1,2));
Set<Bad>  bad  = new HashSet<>(); bad.add(new Bad(1,2));   bad.add(new Bad(1,2));
answer: Objects.hash(x, y)|o instanceof Bad b && b.x == x && b.y == y|bad.size()
explanation: Verified: `1 2`. Both classes report the two objects equal; only one set agrees. `HashSet` finds the bucket by hash code first and only compares within it, so two equal objects with different hashes never meet. Nothing throws and nothing warns — the collection quietly holds a duplicate, which is why the contract is a contract rather than a suggestion.
